messages.subject: question about strip transects
parts:
Greetings list...

I've been doing strip transects for dugong abundance and would =
appreciate some advice on how to set up Distance, and/or how to improve =
this design. As we hope to get a better plane this year, we are hoping =
to use line transects!

As the assumption is that everything is seen within the strip...it seems =
that the uniform detection function is the only model that fits...g(x) =
doesn't change over a set distance. with a 0 adjustment term? =20

the strip width was calculated according to what we could see in the =
water and pieces of cloth tied to the wings as indicators at a fixed =
altitude...
as D=3D (average cluster, size)* (encounter rate)/ (2* effective strip =
width)...then I set the truncation distance as half the estimate width =
of the strip....hopefully that makes sense as well.


thanks in advance for feedback..Ellen

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: question about strip transects
parts: > > As the assumption is that everything is seen within the strip...it

> > seems that the uniform detection function is the only model that
> > fits...g(x) doesn't change over a set distance. with a 0 adjustment
> > term?

That is correct - on the detection function tab of model definition
properties, select the uniform key function. Then click on the adjustment
terms tab, click 'manual selection', and set 'Num adj parameters' to zero.
> > the strip width was calculated according to what we could see in the
> > water and pieces of cloth tied to the wings as indicators at a fixed

> > altitude...
> > as D= (average cluster, size)* (encounter rate)/ (2* effective strip
> > width)...then I set the truncation distance as half the estimate width
> > of the strip....hopefully that makes sense as well.

Yes, that is correct.

I'm glad to see you're planning to try line transect sampling! I've never
believed that it is plausible that detectability doesn't fall off with
distance from the line. Typically, you would use a wider strip when using
line transect sampling, and you'll need to give different training to your
observers on how they search.

Steve
